sn47.11:1.3: The thirty-two “marks of a great man” are detailed in [dn14:1.32.7](), [dn30:1.2.4](), and [mn91:9.1](), while the “meditation of a great man” is said to be emptiness ([mn151:2.6]()). Sāriputta is asking the Buddha to redefine a Vedic term, which is defined in Śāṅkhāyana Āraṇyaka 8.3: “The great man is just the year, of which the sun is the essence. That which is the incorporeal self made of wisdom, and that which is yonder sun are one and the same: so should one understand it.” Thus the great man is the realized soul who understands that he is essentially one with the divine cosmos.
